title: Order reservations behind a rollout flag
name: Order reservation migration

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code switches between the two reservation implementations? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
reservation-v2 is configured with percent=20. How are customers assigned to the new reservation path?
choices: Each create_order call independently has a 20% chance of using V2
The first 20% of orders after the flag is enabled use V2
A given customer is assigned deterministically by a hash of the flag key and customer ID, so new orders from them take the same path while the percentage is unchanged
Customers are assigned by order ID, so the same customer can alternate between paths

questions.prompt: A customer orders two lines, and the second SKU has too little stock under V2. What is the end state?
choices: The order is saved as pending with only the first line reserved
The order is not saved and the first line's hold has been given back
The order is not saved but the first line's units stay unavailable until a cancel
The order is saved as cancelled with both holds released

questions.prompt: An engineer renames the flag in the flag store to "reservation_v2" but not in this service. What do new orders do?
choices: create_order raises because the flag does not exist
All customers get the V2 path because the lookup falls back to enabled
The service logs an error and retries the lookup
All new orders silently use V1
